datum: Heights in metres as served; the service does not state its vertical datum. Against the rover's localisation elevations (Mars geoid) the grid is not a constant shift: see stops_check.route_fifths. Use it for relative height (slope, climb, line of sight), not to restate absolute rover elevations.
source: NASA Mars Trek, Gale_DEM_SMG_1m (MRO HiRISE 1 m elevation model), raw float32 heights resampled by the server (bilinear) to 1552 x 3200 cells
layout: row-major; row 0 = north edge, col 0 = west edge; cell centres at half-cell offsets inside bounds
decode: gunzip; int16 little-endian; first value of a row adds to the first value of the row above (0 above row 0), every other value adds to the value on its left, wrapping in int16; elev_m = q * scale_m + offset_m

stops_check.meaning: this grid minus the rover's localisation elevation, metres (grid interpolated between cell centres)

credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/USGS (MRO HiRISE), served by NASA Mars Trek
